_note: Key path: aspect_character -> guidance_mode -> variant. Variants let the weekly selector avoid reusing the same guidance block in one report.

fallback.v1: Use this moment to notice the pattern before deciding whether it needs action.
fallback.v2: Let this contact clarify what is active, then choose a response small enough to test.
fallback.v3: Treat this as timing information: useful, specific, and not the whole story by itself.
fallback.v4: Let the contact name the active thread without asking it to explain everything.
fallback.v5: Use this as evidence, then wait for the week to show what kind of response it deserves.
fallback.v6: Keep the signal close to lived facts: what changed, what repeated, and what became easier to see?

fallback.v1: Use this moment to accept available support and move the already-open thread one step forward.
fallback.v2: Let the ease become practical. Choose the next step that is already partly available.
fallback.v3: Do not overcomplicate the opening. Give the supported thread one clean action.
fallback.v4: Let the simpler route count. Ease is still information when it is specific.
fallback.v5: Use the opening while it is fresh, before turning it into a problem to solve.
fallback.v6: Move with the part of the pattern that is already cooperating.

action.v1: Use this moment for direct movement: send it, start it, ask it, or test the route while the door is open.
action.v2: Act while the signal is warm, but keep the action small enough to learn from.
action.v3: Let initiative stay concrete here. A visible next step matters more than a perfect plan.
action.v4: Choose the action that can be completed or clearly begun today.
action.v5: Do one thing that gives the momentum somewhere real to go.
action.v6: Let movement answer the question better than more planning would.

receiving.v1: Let support land before you turn it into another responsibility.
receiving.v2: Receive what is available here: ease, attention, help, pleasure, or a wider margin.
receiving.v3: Use this contact to notice what feels genuinely good without immediately justifying it.
receiving.v4: Let the good thing be simple before you make it useful.
receiving.v5: Notice where life offers more room than you expected, and take the room seriously.
receiving.v6: Accept the easier exchange without discounting it as luck.

pacing.v1: Let the body set the tempo. The useful move may be responding sooner, not pushing harder.
pacing.v2: Use this cue to pace the day around what feels naturally available.
pacing.v3: Follow the softer opening without needing it to become a major decision.
pacing.v4: Let timing matter more than force here.
pacing.v5: Check capacity before turning a small opening into a full commitment.
pacing.v6: Respond at the pace the moment can actually hold.

fallback.v1: Use this moment to adjust expectations, name the friction, and choose the next workable step.
fallback.v2: Let the pressure become information before it becomes a verdict.
fallback.v3: Respond to the mismatch directly, but keep the response proportionate to the actual signal.
fallback.v4: Clarify what is tight before deciding what has to change.
fallback.v5: Let the contact show where the old approach has become too expensive.
fallback.v6: Name the friction in plain terms; that alone may reduce its size.

conversation.v1: Say the smaller true sentence before it becomes the larger one.
conversation.v2: Use this contact for clarification: what was meant, what was heard, and what needs cleaner language?
conversation.v3: A direct request or refusal works better here than hints, tests, or private rehearsals.
conversation.v4: Ask the clarifying question before filling in the silence yourself.
conversation.v5: Keep the sentence specific enough that someone else can actually answer it.
conversation.v6: Let the conversation solve one real confusion, not every old one.

structure.v1: Give the pressure a container: a limit, schedule, budget, repair plan, or agreed next step.
structure.v2: The useful response is structural. Make the demand smaller, clearer, and easier to hold.
structure.v3: Do not solve the whole pattern. Build the one support that keeps this contact from spilling everywhere.
structure.v4: Choose the rule, boundary, or sequence that makes the pressure less shapeless.
structure.v5: A practical container will help more than another round of effort.
structure.v6: Let structure do some of the carrying so willpower does not have to do all of it.

discernment.v1: Separate signal from atmosphere before acting on either one.
discernment.v2: Use this contact to verify what is real, what is implied, and what simply needs more time.
discernment.v3: Let uncertainty slow the decision, not erase the meaning.
discernment.v4: Do not make a permanent conclusion from a blurry signal.
discernment.v5: Check the evidence twice: once for facts, once for feeling.
discernment.v6: Let the unclear part stay named as unclear until more evidence arrives.

adjustment.v1: Make the smallest adjustment that changes the pressure without pretending it disappears.
adjustment.v2: Treat the disruption as design feedback: what needs more room, clearer terms, or a different route?
adjustment.v3: Shift the pattern where it is actually tight, not everywhere at once.
adjustment.v4: Change the part of the setup that keeps producing the same snag.
adjustment.v5: Let the interruption point to the outdated assumption.
adjustment.v6: Choose a revision that gives the system more room to move.

visibility.v1: Notice what becomes harder to hide here, then decide how much visibility is actually useful.
visibility.v2: Let the visible pressure clarify the private choice underneath it.
visibility.v3: This contact may ask you to be seen more accurately, not more dramatically.
visibility.v4: Bring the relevant part into view without turning it into a performance.
visibility.v5: Let the exposure be precise: what needs to be known, and by whom?
visibility.v6: Use visibility as information, not as a demand to prove yourself.

fallback.v1: Use this moment to notice the pattern before deciding whether it needs action.
fallback.v2: Let the cue repeat or clarify before you force a conclusion.
fallback.v3: Track what this contact points toward; the useful answer may arrive through sequence.
fallback.v4: Let observation be the work for now.
fallback.v5: Name the cue and keep watching what gathers around it.
fallback.v6: Give the signal enough room to show whether it is passing or important.

visibility.v1: Let one thing become a little more visible without asking it to explain the whole week.
visibility.v2: Use this moment to name what has been sitting in the background.
visibility.v3: Visibility is enough here. Action can wait until the pattern is clearer.
visibility.v4: Notice what wants to be acknowledged, even if it is not ready to be solved.
visibility.v5: Let the visible clue stay modest and still count.
visibility.v6: Use this as a naming moment, not necessarily a doing moment.

pacing.v1: Let the timing cue set the pace rather than forcing an immediate outcome.
pacing.v2: Use this as a rhythm check: what speeds up, what slows down, and what feels easier to carry?
pacing.v3: The moment is useful even if it only changes your tempo.
pacing.v4: Let the day breathe around this cue before choosing a response.
pacing.v5: Adjust the pace first; the meaning may become clearer afterward.
pacing.v6: This contact may be more about timing than decision.
